questions.prompt: Do California's DUI laws apply to medicine prescribed by your doctor?
choices: No, only to alcohol and illegal drugs.
Yes, if it affects your ability to drive.
Only if you take more than the prescribed dose.
questions.explanation: DUI law makes no distinction between illegal drugs and medicines from a doctor or pharmacy. Any drug that impairs your driving counts.

questions.prompt: Is it illegal to drive after taking a large amount of cough syrup that contains alcohol?
choices: Yes; alcohol in any form counts.
No; medicines are exempt from DUI law.
Only if it was not prescribed to you.
questions.explanation: At any age it is illegal to drive after drinking excessive alcohol in any form, including medicines like cough syrup.

questions.prompt: You had one beer and took an allergy pill. Together they make you drowsy. May you drive?
choices: No; their combined effect is what counts.
No; you may never drive after taking any medicine.
Yes; each alone is within safe limits.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive after using any combination of alcohol or drugs that reduces your ability to drive safely. Medicine alone is a problem only if it affects your driving.

questions.prompt: How does your tolerance to alcohol change as you get older?
choices: It decreases.
It increases.
It stays the same.
questions.explanation: Tolerance to alcohol decreases with age, which raises the risk of alcohol-related driving problems.

questions.prompt: An officer who suspects DUI asks you to take a blood test, and you refuse. What happens?
choices: A one-year suspension or revocation.
Nothing, because the test is voluntary.
You get a warning noted on your record.
questions.explanation: If you refuse a required chemical test, the DMV will suspend or revoke your driving privilege for one year.

questions.prompt: A 15-year-old is convicted of riding a bicycle under the influence. What can happen?
choices: Nothing; DUI laws don't cover bicycles.
A fine only, with no effect on driving.
A one-year delay in getting a license.
questions.explanation: If you are 13 to 20 and convicted of bicycling under the influence, your driving privilege may be suspended or delayed for one year once you are eligible.

questions.prompt: You are driving your own car. May your passenger drink a beer or eat a cannabis edible?
choices: No; the rule covers everyone in the car.
No; no alcohol may be in the car at all.
Yes, if the driver is sober.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink alcohol or smoke or eat cannabis while driving or riding as a passenger in a private car. Sealed, unopened containers may be carried.

questions.prompt: In which of these may a passenger have an open container of alcohol?
choices: In the back seat of a car.
In the cab of a pickup.
In a taxi.
questions.explanation: The open-container rules don't apply to passengers in a bus, taxi, camper or motorhome.

questions.prompt: What does BAC (blood alcohol concentration) measure?
choices: How many drinks you have had.
The alcohol in your bloodstream.
How long since your last drink.
questions.explanation: BAC measures how much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.prompt: You are 25. What is the lowest BAC at which it is illegal for you to drive?
questions.explanation: Drivers over 21 may not drive with a BAC of 0.08% or higher.

questions.prompt: You are 19. What is the lowest BAC at which it is illegal for you to drive?
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 may not drive with a BAC of 0.01% or higher.

questions.prompt: A 35-year-old is on DUI probation. What is the lowest BAC at which it is illegal for them to drive?
questions.explanation: At any age, if you are on DUI probation, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.01% or higher.

questions.prompt: When you drive a passenger for hire, what is the lowest BAC at which driving is illegal?
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.04% or higher when driving a passenger for hire or a vehicle that needs a commercial license.

questions.prompt: Your BAC is below the legal limit. Is it safe to drive?
choices: Not necessarily; alcohol affects you below it.
Yes; the limit is set at the safe level for all.
Yes, as long as you feel completely fine.
questions.explanation: A BAC below the limit doesn't mean it's safe. Almost everyone feels effects of alcohol even below the limit.

questions.prompt: Can you be convicted of DUI without a BAC measurement?
choices: Yes, depending on how impaired you are.
No, a BAC reading is always required.
Only if you refused to be tested.
questions.explanation: You can be arrested and convicted of DUI based on how impaired you are, even without a BAC measurement.

questions.prompt: Which of these affects how high your BAC rises from drinking?
choices: How long you have been driving.
The time of day you drink.
Your body weight and gender.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how many drinks you have, your gender and your body weight.

questions.prompt: What is the fewest drinks that can affect your ability to drive safely?
choices: Three.
One.
Enough to reach 0.08%.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.prompt: You are about to ride a jet ski on a lake. What does the law say about drinking alcohol?
choices: You may not drink while you operate it.
You may drink, since you're off the road.
You may drink if you stay under 0.08%.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink alcohol or take drugs while operating a boat, jet ski, water skis or similar vessel.

questions.prompt: By driving in California, what have you agreed to?
choices: A search of your car at any traffic stop.
A breath test at any traffic stop at all.
A chemical test if suspected of DUI.
questions.explanation: By driving in California you consent to a breath, blood or urine test if an officer suspects DUI.

questions.prompt: You took a breath test after being stopped for DUI. May you still be required to take a blood or urine test?
choices: No, one test is the limit.
Yes, to check for drugs.
Only if your breath test was over 0.08%.
questions.explanation: Even after a preliminary screening or breath test, you may have to take a blood or urine test to detect drugs.

questions.prompt: Under the Administrative Per Se law, what happens when you are arrested for DUI?
choices: Nothing, until a court convicts you.
You get a warning letter from the DMV.
The DMV suspends your driving privilege.
questions.explanation: Administrative Per Se requires the DMV to suspend your driving privilege when you are arrested for DUI, separate from any court case.

questions.prompt: After a DUI arrest, the officer takes your license. What may you be given?
choices: A 30-day temporary license.
A 10-day temporary license.
A 6-month restricted license.
questions.explanation: The officer may take your license and give you a 30-day temporary driver's license.

questions.prompt: After a DUI arrest, how long do you have to request a DMV administrative hearing?
choices: 10 days from the arrest.
30 days from the arrest.
5 days from the arrest.
questions.explanation: You may request a DMV hearing within 10 days of the date of your arrest.

questions.prompt: If you are convicted of DUI, what must you complete?
choices: A traffic violator school course.
A DUI program.
A new behind-the-wheel test.
questions.explanation: A DUI conviction requires you to complete a DUI program.

questions.prompt: After a DUI conviction, which form must you file with the DMV?
choices: An SR-1 traffic collision report.
A DS 699 driver reexamination request.
An SR 22 insurance proof certificate.
questions.explanation: After a DUI conviction you must file a California Insurance Proof Certificate (SR 22/SR 1P), and the DMV will suspend or revoke your license.

questions.prompt: After a DUI conviction, what may you be required to install on your vehicle?
choices: A speed-limiting device.
An ignition interlock device.
A dashboard camera.
questions.explanation: A DUI conviction may require you to install an ignition interlock device (IID).

questions.prompt: A DUI conviction can bring a jail sentence of up to:
choices: Six months.
30 days.
Two years.
questions.explanation: A DUI conviction can mean up to six months in jail, along with fines and other penalties.

questions.prompt: How long does a DUI conviction stay on your driver's record?
choices: 36 months.
Five years.
10 years.
questions.explanation: DUI convictions stay on your record for 10 years, and another DUI in that time can bring added penalties.

questions.prompt: You are 19 and not working. When may you carry alcohol in your car?
choices: Any time the container is sealed and unopened.
Only when it is locked in the trunk.
Only with someone 21 or older, sealed.
questions.explanation: Under 21, you may carry alcohol only with someone 21 or older present, and it must be sealed, or kept in the trunk if opened.

questions.prompt: A driver under 21 is caught with alcohol in the car. How long can the car be impounded?
choices: Up to 10 days.
Up to 30 days.
Up to one year.
questions.explanation: Law enforcement can impound the vehicle for up to 30 days.

questions.prompt: A driver under 21 caught with alcohol in the car may have their license suspended for:
choices: 30 days.
Six months.
One year.
questions.explanation: The court may fine the driver and suspend their license for one year, or delay a first license by up to a year.

questions.prompt: An officer suspects a 19-year-old driver has been drinking. What can the officer require?
choices: A breath test or other chemical test.
Nothing, without proof of a 0.08% BAC.
A field walking test, but no breath test.
questions.explanation: If an officer suspects a driver under 21 has been drinking, they can require a hand-held breath test, PAS, or other chemical test.

questions.prompt: A later test shows a 19-year-old driver's BAC is 0.05%. What may happen?
choices: Arrest for DUI and license suspension.
Nothing, since it is under 0.08%.
A warning, since it is a first stop.
questions.explanation: A driver under 21 whose BAC tests at 0.05% or higher may be arrested for DUI and have their driving privilege suspended.

questions.prompt: A driver under 21 is convicted of DUI with a BAC of 0.01% or more. What may happen?
choices: A 30-day suspension and no DUI program.
A fine only, since it's under 0.08%.
One-year revocation and a DUI program.
questions.explanation: The DMV may revoke the driving privilege for one year, and the driver must complete a licensed DUI program.
